reasons: No test or other evidence of correct behaviour is visible in this file.
Status values are compared as plain text, so a new server status would show as pending without a warning.
Empty lists and failed statuses are handled and shown as failed.

terms.meaning: A reusable piece of the screen, written as a function, that draws part of the page.
One recorded step of the agent's work, such as a query, a page read or a result.
One named phase of a run, such as a single research step.
A function the component calls to tell its parent something happened.
A word the server stores to say how a stage ended, such as succeeded or failed.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Setup
sections.what: Imports the React tools for timing, memory and element references that the view uses.
sections.why: Needed for the timed reveal, the stored values and scrolling.

sections.name: ProcessTraceLine
sections.title: Shape of one trace line
sections.what: Defines one line of the agent's trace: its time, its kind (step, read, code, result or warning), and its text.
sections.why: Gives every trace line one shape so the view can style and order them.
sections.watch_out: Only these five kinds have a symbol and colour, so a new kind needs both added.

sections.name: ProcessStage, GLYPH
sections.title: Shape of one stage
sections.what: Defines one stage with its key, label, purpose, status, trace lines and optional progress text.
sections.why: Sets what each stage must provide to appear in the view.
sections.watch_out: Status is free text, so a misspelled status silently shows as pending.

sections.name: TONE, Flat
sections.title: Symbols and colours by line kind
sections.what: Maps each trace kind to a symbol and a text colour, and defines a helper type that pairs a line with its stage position.
sections.why: Makes each kind of line recognisable at a glance.
sections.watch_out: Symbol and colour are chosen by kind only, so changing one usually needs the other changed too.

sections.name: AgentProcess (part 1)
sections.title: Reveal timing and completion
sections.what: Builds the flat list of lines and reveals them on a timer, working out whether anything is still waiting or running and calling the completion callback once everything is shown.
sections.why: The timer paces the replay so lines appear progressively, and the callback tells the parent screen to show results.
sections.watch_out: The callback is guarded by a flag, so it never fires a second time even if the stages change later.

sections.name: AgentProcess (part 2)
sections.title: Stage status and layout
sections.what: Works out each stage's shown status (pending, active, done or failed) from how many lines are visible and its server status, then draws the stage list, progress bar, header and scrolling trace.
sections.why: A stage shows as done only once its lines are visible, so the view never gets ahead of the reader.
sections.watch_out: A stage with no trace lines moves straight to its server status, so it can change without any animation.

summary: Shows an animated, read-only view of the steps an agent took during a run, one stage at a time.
purpose: Lets a visitor follow the work of a Lessons Learnt or Reality Scan run as a list of stages and a scrolling trace.
why: Likely reason: one view serves both a live run and a finished run, so lines are revealed gradually and only stored lines are shown.
how: Flattens every stage's trace lines into one list. A timer reveals a few lines at a time, faster when more are waiting. A stage counts as done only after all its lines are shown and its server status is succeeded. The left column lists stages with status dots and a progress bar. The right panel shows the active stage, its purpose, and the revealed lines with the newest kept in view. When everything is shown and nothing is running, it calls the completion callback once.
inputs: A list of stages, each with its trace lines and status, plus a title, optional pause and speed settings, and an optional completion callback.
outputs: A rendered two-column view. The only thing sent back is the completion callback.
risks: A stage whose status stays running or queued keeps the view in waiting mode indefinitely. The completion callback fires once per mount, so later changes do not trigger it again.
debug: If the view never finishes, check whether any stage stays in running or queued in the stage data. If lines are missing, check the trace list of each stage. If the completion callback never fires, check that the stage list is not empty.
